question: __________ are known as the powerhouse of the cell.
solution:
The correct answer is **Mitochondria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which is used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are involved in other tasks such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death, as well as maintaining control of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from ancient symbiotic bacteria.
 
• They are double-membrane-bound organelles, with the inner membrane being highly folded into structures known as cristae.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: Nucleus
 The nucleus is the control center of the cell, containing most of the cell's genetic material.
 
 

 Option 2: Cytoplasm
 The cytoplasm is the gel-like substance within the cell membrane, containing all organelles and cell parts.
 
 

 Option 3: Mitochondria
 Mitochondria generate ATP and are involved in various other cellular processes.
 
 

 Option 4: Endoplasmic Reticulum
 The endoplasmic reticulum is involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
